title: Inspect and maintain the Semantics installation
summary: Understand readiness, serial worker scheduling, run-owned admission, exact release publication, state migration, rollback, recovery, and retained-state uninstall.
use_when: Semantics readiness, maintenance, installation ownership, migration, recovery, or worker failure policy must be understood.
The selected release, provider, binding, enabled intent, or retained transaction should be verified.
do_not_use_when: Only maintained terminology or project lifecycle is the subject.
Uninstall is being used as authority to erase retained state.
outcome: A selected, ownership-checked user installation or retained recovery condition whose admission, scheduler, persistent-state, and publication guarantees remain explicit.

interfaces.label: Maintenance admission
interfaces.invocation: semantics --database DATABASE --json maintenance status; semantics --database DATABASE --json maintenance hold RUN_ID; semantics --database DATABASE --json maintenance release RUN_ID

effects: Installation writes a content-addressed release including complete provider bytes, publishes owned selectors, registers/selects the exact worker, and may initialize or migrate SQLite under proved quiescence.
Run-owned admission gates fence public commands before state access; installer markers also fence pinned runners and frontends.
Uninstall removes owned public scheduling/command/provider selection and retains state, releases, definitions, history, and logs.

Installation performs resource setup, configuration, initialization or migration, and publication under the operation's maintenance hold. It does not invoke doctor or gate completion on persistent-state validation or runtime readiness. Ordinary runtime checks and diagnostics remain separate.
authority: Semantics owns program/provider selection, state migrations, update and worker locks, product holds, readiness checks, and product recovery.
Clockwork owns scheduled activation, process history, incident halts and notification; Nucleus owns runtime evidence. Shared coordination retains each product commit boundary.
success: Deployment holds and drains affected work, stages files, configures and publishes selected products, releases only its own holds, and restores captured activation intent. It preserves data, operator pauses, and incident halts.
failure_and_recovery: Foreign/changed artifacts, unsafe state files, unavailable existing runtime, or unknown ownership fail closed.

Pre-commit rollback restores selectors and at most one prior scheduler when the database schema is unchanged. Live data remains in place. Schema changes require forward recovery; unproved recovery retains maintenance and transaction evidence.
Committed transactions recover forward. Prior-null selected-candidate recovery requires explicit --forward for the authenticated exact candidate.
privacy: State can contain complete private documents, meanings, paths, correlations, and history.
Clockwork receives exact program/schedule/process and bounded incident metadata; it does not read product log bodies.
does_not_authorize: Clearing another owner hold or marker, resetting project pause/incident halt, canceling or retrying durable work implicitly, concurrent direct binding mutation, or retained-state deletion.

consumers.statement: Local operators, the product installer, and the Cell deployment adapter inspect and maintain one current-user Semantics installation.

preconditions.statement: Effects require authorized matching candidates, proved owned selectors/files and worker/database quiescence, and compatible dependencies. Unsupported old public admission needs its documented compatibility release first.

inputs.statement: Inputs are exact candidate binary/provider/Clockwork artifacts, selected private state, captured scheduler intent and ownership, run-owned holds, optional explicit final legacy watermark, or one retained transaction.

outputs.statement: Doctor returns typed checks; maintenance returns protocol_version 1, contract_version 1, holds and drained; installer receipts, retained transaction, exact release selectors, and selected definition describe the installation outcome.

data_semantics.statement: Readiness, live-command drain, durable-job quiescence, runtime exit, semantic success, enabled intent, operator pause, maintenance, and incident halt are distinct observations or controls.

identity_and_units.statement: Content release identity covers runner/template/provider bytes; definition digest pins exact runner/schedule; maintenance owner ID identifies only its own durable hold; database schema and contracts are independently versioned.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Doctor checks one fixed Annals watermark and repeats complete bounded pages from each distinct cursor through unchanged empty, rejecting more than 1,000 pages per cursor. A selected definition ownership check is point-in-time, not compare-and-swap. Drain covers live admitted commands and requires separate durable-job proof.
No launchd availability, worker wake-up latency, or source-to-revision deadline is promised.

access.statement: Current-user local interfaces and owned private files are the trust boundary. Existing state/receipt/log shapes and permissions are checked; catalog queries are not runtime readiness or authorization.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Installation performs resource setup, configuration, initialization or migration, and publication under the operation's maintenance hold. It does not invoke doctor or gate completion on persistent-state validation or runtime readiness. Ordinary runtime checks and diagnostics remain separate.

A public run hold fences all other public/typed commands before database access, survives exit, and releases only its owner. Installer markers/receipts have separate exact ownership. Group activation preserves captured intent, project pauses, and incident halts.

operational_limits.statement: The worker requests 60-second interval, no run-at-load, overlap skip, no timeout, exact interpreter/runner hashes and scrubbed environment. Only one reconciliation is processed per serial pass.
No throughput, storage capacity, service response objective, retention horizon, or future support/deprecation window is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: SQLite schema 3 preserves legacy and account history, source/cursor bytes, receipts and admitted immutable requests. Explicit one-time activation is separate from ordinary updates. Provider schema 4 adds overview publication without changing runtime behavior or old entry versions.

reliances.statement: The separate runtime doctor checks the selected Annals decisions feed and library through exchange 2. Installation does not replay the feed.
Nucleus supplies runtime/drain, health, capabilities and retained job evidence; a held proof requires the same sole drained run owner.

Clockwork owns immutable definitions, selected binding, scheduled process activation and the shared service-health delay before a new halt. By default, five consecutive failed read-only checks, at least 60 seconds apart, establish the halt and alert eligibility together. Later activations remain admissible before that threshold; healthy or inactive checks clear a pending episode. Established halts require exact approval. Domain retry and uncertain Nucleus correlation remain Semantics-owned.
Semantics promises no launchd availability or wake-up latency beyond Clockwork observations.
